Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acme is close to selecting a preferred inference partner. The security team had a few targeted questions to close out our SIG spreadsheet. Would you mind confirming the items below? I attached the latest SIG XLSX with highlighted rows.

1) Data retention: what are Redwood's default retention periods for request logs, prompt text (including partial prompts/sessions), and generated outputs? Can customers configure shorter/longer retention per contract or per-tenant setting?

2) Prompt/log storage: are prompt texts ever persisted to long-term object storage? If so, where (region) and what safeguards (encryption, access controls) are applied?

3) Model training: do you ever use customer-provided content to further train Redwood internal models or third-party model weights? If so, is this opt-in only and how is it documented/contracted?

If you can provide a short matrix + any supporting artifacts (SOC 2 control mapping, policy excerpts, or a single-page answer doc) that would help us move to procurement. Our deadline for the final SIG is EOD May 21.

Hannah / Marcus — draft answers below. I've attached the PDF export (redwood_sig_response_20260518.pdf) and cited the relevant internal SOP and SOC 2 control references in the comments. Please review and flag anything legal should consider.

Summary (short answers):
- Default retention: request logs and telemetry are retained for 30 days by default. Customer-specific data (uploaded files, attachments) are retained per the customer's configured retention policy; default is 30 days.
- Configurability: Customers on Dedicated and Private deployments can configure retention windows from 0 (no retention) up to 730 days via contractual Addendum. Hosted customers can request changes via support/contract.
- Prompt text storage: Prompt text and generated outputs are stored transiently in the KV cache and application logs; persistent archival to object storage does not occur by default for hosted customers. Long-term storage in object storage is only used when a customer explicitly enables log export or enables audit logging to their own S3/GCS bucket.
- Protections: All stored logs and exported archives are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Access is restricted via RBAC and audited. Customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations are available for Private and Dedicated deployments.
- Training on customer data: Redwood DOES NOT use customer-provided content to further train or fine-tune internal or public models unless explicitly agreed in writing (opt-in). Any programmatic training or model updates that involve customer content require: (1) a signed Data Training Addendum, (2) obvious opt-in in the customer console or contract, and (3) ability to opt-out and delete datasets.

Controls / Evidence pointers:
- SOC 2: CC6 & CC7 mapping (see attached PDF page 3) — retention and encryption controls described.
- Audit logs: we can provide sample audit log extracts and describe the export process; however, production audit logs are not shared without a legal process.

Attachment: redwood_sig_response_20260518.pdf (pdf)

Notes for Hannah: I avoided legal wording about unlimited retention; kept language conservative and contract-forward. Dev, please sign off on the "Data Training Addendum" wording before we send externally.
